content:
We have been running iOS 27 for two months now. It is, of course, still in beta and probably four to six weeks away from a public release. But even though I've had the beta running on my phone for the past two months, I barely know it's there. It just... works.

Of course, I still rush to the Software Update screen every few weeks to install the latest beta build. That's the one constant of the beta experience across cycle number 27.

Beyond that, I can't think of the usual beta issues. Battery drain is basically nonexistent, the phone doesn't get hot, and there's no rogue bug or random SpringBoard resprings.

iOS 27 lets you enjoy all the perks of new software — Siri AI, AirPods EQ, new Wallet passes in Safari, beefier Photos AI edits and more — without any of the typical pitfalls of running the leading-edge beta. Honestly, it's a little surprising.

It may also have something to do with iOS 26 being unstable right out of the gate. iOS 26.5 in particular was, somehow (at least for me), responsible for constant resprings.

Of course, this is all anecdotal, but ask just about anyone and you'll hear similar stories about iOS 26 not being great for them either.

iOS 27 is legitimately delivering

Overall, iOS 27 delivers when it comes to speed improvements, bug fixes, stability and overall quality of life. You may not notice it right away because Siri AI is doing a lot of background indexing — but Apple rolled out iOS 26.6, so by the time you jump up to iOS 27, it's already started indexing in the background for Siri AI and you don't have to do anything. Smooth sailing from there.

Top comment by Uno

While I broadly agree that the iOS 27 (and WatchOS 27) betas are noticeably more stable and less battery hungry than iOS betas of yesteryear, I have to push back on the Siri portion. In the two iOS/WatchOS 27 betas released so far, Siri is basically unusable. Typing in the Siri app is fine, but using voice is so incredibly frustrating that it is a complete waste of time.

This is, of course, strictly anecdotal.

I am very much looking forward to iOS 27's public rollout next month. It's a little hard to believe, but Apple may have actually addressed most of the major pain points in iOS. Software is never going to be perfect — but this is absolutely the smoothest my iPhone has run that I can remember in recent memory.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone model capable of running iOS 26, all the way back to the iPhone 11 and beyond.
